description: A genuinely quiet overnight for an engineering manager: automated deploys, a resolved incident, and colleagues answering each other. Nothing is owed by the user. The failure mode is inventing an obligation out of a thread that merely mentions them.

events.text: Deployed api-gateway v4.19.2 to production. 0 failed health checks. Rollback token dp-88213.
Paged for elevated 5xx on the search endpoint. Looking now, will update in 15.
Found it — a bad cache key from the v4.19.2 rollout. Reverted the key format, errors back to baseline. No customer reports. I'll write it up in the morning, nothing needed from anyone tonight.
Does anyone know why the nightly index job takes 40 minutes now? It was 12 last month.
It's the new embeddings column — we're reindexing the whole table instead of the delta. I opened PLAT-812 and I'll take it this sprint. Answered, no action needed from anyone else.

events.context_label: Weekly engineering digest — no reply needed
events.text: This week across engineering: 41 pull requests merged, 3 incidents (all resolved), and the platform team shipped the new indexing pipeline. This digest is informational; replies are not monitored.

acceptable_briefings: What moved: api-gateway v4.19.2 went to production. Quietly resolved: Nadia traced elevated search 5xx to a bad cache key from that rollout and reverted it, with no customer reports; Ruth identified the slow nightly index job as a full reindex caused by the new embeddings column and took PLAT-812. Nothing is waiting on you.
Nothing needs you. Overnight: a clean api-gateway deploy, a search 5xx incident Nadia found and fixed, and a slow index job Ruth diagnosed and picked up.
supported_claims: api-gateway v4.19.2 was deployed to production with no failed health checks.
Nadia traced elevated search 5xx errors to a bad cache key from the v4.19.2 rollout and reverted it.
There were no customer reports from the search incident.
Ruth identified the nightly index slowdown as a full reindex caused by the new embeddings column and opened PLAT-812.
Ruth said she would take PLAT-812 this sprint.
unsupported_claims: You need to review the incident write-up.
Nadia is waiting for your approval to revert the cache key change.
You need to decide who takes PLAT-812.
You are expected to reply to the engineering digest.
ground_truth.notes: Precision fixture. Every thread here closes itself: Nadia both found and fixed the incident and said so explicitly, Ruth both diagnosed and claimed the index issue, and the digest states replies are not monitored. A manager is MENTIONED-adjacent throughout without being asked for anything, which is exactly the shape that produces a false pending item — 'incident happened' reads like 'manager must review'. The correct answer is an empty Waiting-on-you section.
